answer: Posted collateral must equal 4 times the reward claimed, so ambition is priced rather than free. Because the echo collateral is checked against the yarrow claim at intake, the mirror audit records the ratio and an under-collateralised submission is refused. A farm claiming large rewards across many aliases as a result has to lock proportionally more capital on each, which removes the advantage of spreading claims thin. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
